header: I keep these plain-code guards on what the model writes. They came from the Zero Tolerance answer (11 Nov 2026), and all of them are general:

1. fixDiscretionIssuers: an authority the circular names only as the holder of a DISCRETION ("... / Discretion of Head of Safety") is not the one who ISSUES. The model put "Head of Safety" in the "Issued through" column and dropped the words "Discretion of". Where every place the circular names that authority is "discretion of <authority>", I make the issuer cell say "Not stated in circular" and put the words back into the consequence cell (the cell just left of the issuer column), where the circular has them.

2. stripUnsupportedForce: "immediately", "automatically", "directly", "instantly" add speed or force the circular did not write ("the penalty is imposed DIRECTLY on the contractor" for "imposed on the contractor"). When the circulars never use the word, I take it out of a sentence (the rest of the sentence is untouched). A word the circular uses is left alone.

3. fixItemCount: the overview said "Ten distinct schemes are compared" over a table of twelve (Motivational Award Schemes answer, 11 Nov 2026). A count the text gives for the items the table COMPARES must be the table's own row count: I say it in the table's own noun (its first column's header or its title: "Name of the Scheme" -> "schemes"), only in the plain shapes "<count> <noun> are compared/listed/covered ..." and "compares/lists/covers <count> <noun>". I never touch any other number in the text (grades, rupees, "three for executives").

4. restoreTruncatedAbbreviations: "900 sq. f." for the circular's "sq. ft." (a model slip, 11 Nov 2026). Two abbreviations in a row whose second is a CUT form of a longer abbreviation that the circulars print after the same first one ("sq. ft.", "Asst. Mgr.", "Dy. Gen.") go back to the circular's form. I do this only when the circulars never print the cut form, print exactly one longer form, and that form adds at most three letters. Any other text is never touched.

symbols.name: stripUnsupportedForce
symbols.sig: export function stripUnsupportedForce(text: string, sourceText: string): { text: string; removed: string[] }
doc: I take out the force words the circulars never use. Returns the text and the words removed.

symbols.name: tableNouns
doc: Returns the singular forms of the nouns the table is made of: the first column's header and the title ("Name of the Scheme", "Motivational Award Schemes of DSP" -> scheme, award, motivational).

symbols.name: fixItemCount
symbols.sig: export function fixItemCount(text: string, table: SynthesisTable | null | undefined): { text: string; changed: string[] }

symbols.name: restoreTruncatedAbbreviations
symbols.sig: export function restoreTruncatedAbbreviations(text: string, sourceText: string): { text: string; changed: string[] }
doc: In one text I put a cut abbreviation that follows another abbreviation back as the circulars print it.

symbols.name: mapBriefingTexts
symbols.sig: export function mapBriefingTexts(r: SynthesisResult, fix: (t: string) => string): SynthesisResult
doc: I apply `fix` to every text of the briefing (overview, headline, findings, tables, charts). I do not change the result in place.

symbols.name: restoreAllAbbreviations
symbols.sig: export function restoreAllAbbreviations(r: SynthesisResult, sourceText: string): { result: SynthesisResult; changed: string[] }
doc: Restores the cut abbreviations in every text of a briefing. I do not change the result in place.

symbols.name: normaliseIdentifiers
symbols.sig: export function normaliseIdentifiers(r: SynthesisResult): { result: SynthesisResult; changed: string[] }
doc: I take the separators out of identifiers (account, policy, cheque numbers) in every text of a briefing: src/lib/ui/identifiers.ts. The result is not changed in place.

symbols.name: fixUnprintedNotApplicable
symbols.sig: export function fixUnprintedNotApplicable(r: SynthesisResult, sourceText: string): { result: SynthesisResult; changed: number }
doc: My view: "Not applicable" is a claim. A table cell that says a case does not apply says something the circular must say; a case the circular's table merely does not list (an item given for one duration only, a row given for one grade) is "Not stated in circular", not "Not applicable". When the circulars nowhere print "not applicable", "N/A", "not allowed", "not permitted", "nil" or the like, I turn a cell "Not applicable" into "Not stated in circular".

the words go back into the consequence cell, inside its own condition bracket
a real issuer (the circular says 'through concerned CGM/HOD') is left alone
the original table is not changed
a consequence cell with no condition gets the words as a condition
an authority the circular names elsewhere as the one who issues is kept
an authority not found in the circulars at all is not this guard's business
a table with no issuer column is left alone
after the guard, the 'who issues' finding no longer names the discretion holder as an issuer
an issuer cell that itself reads 'Discretion of X' is moved out too, and the words join the condition
'directly' is taken out when the circular does not say it
'immediately' goes with its comma spacing intact
a word the circular uses is left alone
the word 'director' is not mistaken for 'directly'
a sentence that starts with the word is left as it is
text with none of the words is untouched
'Ten distinct schemes are compared' over 12 rows becomes Twelve, bold and capital kept
'compares 10 schemes' becomes 12 in digits
a count that is already right is left alone
a number that does not count the compared items is never touched
a count of something other than the table's items is left alone
rows that repeat their first cell are not counted as items
no table, or one row: nothing
the engine runs the count guard on the overview and the findings

the prompt carries both rules
'sq. f.' becomes the circular's 'sq. ft.'
a form the circulars print as written is not touched
a cut form with no longer form in the circulars is not touched
an initial after a title the circulars print the same way is not touched
two different longer forms in the circulars: not sure, not touched
capitals are kept
every text of the briefing is read: overview, findings, table cells and headings, chart title, subtitle and items
the engine runs it on every candidate, and the writer is told a condition belongs to its rows only
account, policy and cheque numbers lose their separators in the overview, the findings and the cells
a sum of money keeps its grouping
the engine runs it on every candidate and again after the second reading, and the writer is told
a cell 'Not applicable' the circulars never say becomes 'Not stated in circular'
when the circulars say 'not applicable' the cell is left alone
the engine runs it, and an unnamed two-series chart is not shown
